items.title: Section: Still Sharing Rewards With Servants Long Past Their Prime

items.zh: 又諸臣等年耆衰邁，曾於長夜供奉侍衛，雖知無勢、無力、無勇，然念昔恩，轉懷敬愛，而不輕賤，爵祿、勳庸分賞無替。如是名王善知差別知所作恩。云何名王不自縱任不行放逸？謂有國王，於妙五欲而不沈沒、耽著嬉戲、愛樂受行，能於時時勗勵方便作所應作，勞賚群臣。如是名王不自縱任不行放逸。若王成就如是功德，雖無大府庫、無大輔佐、無大軍眾，而可歸仰。大王當知！如是十種王之功德，初一名為種姓功德，餘九名為自性功德。
items.en: And ministers now aged and enfeebled, who once served him faithfully through long years of attendance, though known to lack influence, strength, and vigour, are still remembered with kindness, treated with growing respect and affection rather than contempt, and continue to share without fail in whatever rank, salary, and reward is properly theirs. This is called skilfully distinguishing worthy ministers while remembering kindness received. What is called a king's freedom from heedless self-indulgence? A king never sunk in the five exquisite pleasures, able to rouse himself again and again to his own proper duties and reward his ministers. This is called freedom from heedless self-indulgence. If a king possesses such virtues, though he lacks a great treasury, great ministers, and a great army, he yet deserves reliance. Great King, you should know that of these ten virtues, the first is the virtue of lineage, and the remaining nine are virtues of character.

items.zh: 云何名為王衰損門？大王當知！王衰損門略有五種。

items.title: Section: Ministers Who Learn to Hide Their Own Talent

items.zh: 一、不善觀察而攝群臣；二、雖善觀察而攝群臣，無恩妙行，縱有非時；三、專行放逸，不思機務；四、專行放逸，不守府庫；五、專行放逸，不修法行。如是五種皆悉名為王衰損門。云何名王不善觀察而攝群臣？謂有國王，於群臣等不能究察、不審究察、不能思擇、不審思擇，忠信、伎藝、智慧差別，攝為親侍，加以寵愛，厚賜爵祿，重賞勳庸，最機密處而相委任，數以軟言現為慰諭。然此群臣，所付財寶多有損費。若遇怨敵、惡友、軍陣，彼先退敗，恐懼破散為他所勝，遲留人後，奔北無戀，矯行惡策，動𮓪王政。如是名王不善觀察而攝群臣。云何名王雖善觀察而攝群臣，無恩妙行，縱有非時？謂有國王，雖於群臣性能究察、能審究察、性能思擇、能審思擇，忠信、伎藝、智慧差別，攝為親侍，而不寵愛，不如其量具賜爵祿，最機密處亦不委任，不數軟言現相慰諭。後於一時，王遇怨敵、惡友、軍陣，廣說乃至大怖畏事命難現前，爾時於臣方行寵愛，廣說乃至數以軟言而相慰諭。時群臣等共相謂曰：王於今者危迫因緣，方於我等暫行妙行，非長久心。知此事已，雖有忠信、伎藝、智慧，隱而不現。
items.en: First, taking in ministers without careful observation. Second, carefully observing and taking in ministers, yet with no genuine kindness, favour coming only at the wrong time. Third, heedless indulgence, neglecting important affairs. Fourth, heedless indulgence, failing to guard the treasury. Fifth, heedless indulgence, neglecting the practice of the Dharma. A king who cannot investigate, cannot carefully investigate, cannot deliberate, and cannot carefully deliberate on his ministers' loyalty, skill, and wisdom, yet takes them as close confidants, favouring them, granting them rich rank and reward, entrusting them with the most sensitive matters, and constantly comforting them with gentle words — such ministers squander much of the wealth entrusted to them, and, facing an enemy, a bad friend, or battle, retreat first in fear, broken and overcome by another. The ministers say to one another: the king, only now under threat, briefly treats us well, with no lasting sincerity. Knowing this, though loyal, skilled, and wise, they conceal it and do not show it.

items.zh: 如是名王雖善觀察而攝群臣，無恩妙行，縱有非時。云何名王專行放逸，不思機務？

items.title: Section: A Treasury Emptied by Gambling and Idle Entertainment

items.zh: 謂有國王，於應和好所作所成機務等事，而不時時獨處空閑，或與智者共正思惟、稱量、觀察和好方便。如是於應乖絕所作所成機務等事，於應惠施所作所成機務等事，於應軍陣所作所成機務等事，於應攝受大力朋黨所作所成機務等事，皆不時時獨處空閑，或與智者共正思惟、稱量、觀察乖絕方便，乃至攝受強黨方便。如是名王專行放逸，不思機務。云何名王專行放逸，不守府庫？謂有國王，寡營事業、拙營事業、不持事業、不觀事業，不禁王門、不禁宮門、不禁府庫，或於俳優、伎樂、笑弄、倡逸等所，或復耽樂博弈戲等，非量損費所有財寶。如是名王專行放逸不守府庫。
items.en: A king who, regarding affairs that call for conciliation, and, likewise, affairs that call for severance, affairs that call for charity, affairs that call for military deployment, and affairs that call for drawing in powerful factions, does not regularly set aside quiet time alone, or with the wise, to properly reflect on, weigh, and examine the means of conciliation, down through the means of drawing in powerful factions. This is called a king's heedless indulgence, neglecting important affairs. What is called a king's heedless indulgence, failing to guard the treasury? A king who manages affairs sparsely, clumsily, without oversight, without attention, failing to secure the palace gate, the inner gate, or the treasury, whether amid entertainers, musicians, jesters, and dancers, or indulging in gambling and games, squandering his treasury's wealth entirely out of proportion. This is called heedless indulgence, failing to guard the treasury.

items.zh: 云何名王專行放逸，不修法行？

blocks.text: The last virtues, and the five ways a kingdom declines.
The good king keeps sharing rewards with servants long past their prime. Master Cháng Bǎi: of the ten virtues, lineage cannot be changed; the other nine are character, which can keep improving.

The first two gates of decline concern how ministers are taken in; the last three begin with heedless indulgence. Master Cháng Bǎi: such ministers waste the wealth entrusted to them and scatter before a battle starts. Only in danger does the king notice his ministers.
Master Cháng Bǎi: he does not reflect from time to time in a quiet place or with the wise. Through board games and gambling, he consumes the treasury.
"Lineage cannot be changed; the other nine virtues can." Most of what makes a good leader is learnable.

quiz.q: The ten virtues fall into two groups. How do they differ, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: all ten flow from birth and cannot be learned, which is why they are called inherent virtues
the virtue of lineage cannot be changed, while the nine virtues of character can keep improving
five of lineage and five of character
lineage can change, character cannot
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the first is the virtue of lineage, one's family background, which cannot be changed; the other nine are virtues of character that can keep being improved. So nine of the ten lie within a ruler's own effort.

quiz.q: How many of the five gateways of decline begin with heedless indulgence, and what does each neglect?
options: all five, for the text marks even the taking in of ministers as heedless indulgence
two, the treasury and the Dharma
one, the Dharma alone
three, neglecting important affairs, the treasury, and the practice of the Dharma
quiz.why: The first two gateways concern how ministers are taken in; the last three all begin with heedless indulgence. Master Cháng Bǎi on the third: busy with the five sense pleasures, the king neglects vital government affairs, and much that should be done is left undone.

quiz.q: When a king favours ministers without examining them, how do they behave?
options: gratitude makes them more loyal still, the only cost being a little wealth
they rebel at once
they quietly resign
they squander the wealth entrusted to them and, facing an enemy or battle, are first to retreat
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: these ministers mostly waste the wealth entrusted to them, and lose courage and scatter before the battle even starts. The treatise names no rebellion here; the fault is unfitness shown when wealth and danger test them.

quiz.q: Why, per Master Cháng Bǎi, do ministers hide their abilities? (The English omits the second gateway's explanation, so two gateways run together.)
options: they truly lack ability and hide that fact, so this belongs to the first gateway
the king is kind only in danger, without lasting sincerity, so they withhold their loyalty and talents
they fear being recruited abroad
the law forbids it
quiz.why: The English lacks the second gateway's explanation, so this passage seems to continue the first. Master Cháng Bǎi: only in danger does the king notice his ministers and treat them a little better, without lasting intent, so they hide their abilities.

quiz.q: 皆不時時獨處空閑 is rendered "never sets aside quiet time alone." What is the difference?
options: none: 不時時 means not once, a heedless king never reflecting, and the lecture reads it so
空閑 should be "vacation"
the text says not regularly, while the English says never, which overstates it
"alone" should be deleted
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: he does not often reflect in a quiet place or with the wise. 不時時 means not from time to time, not "never." §11's "never giving charity" has the same problem, whereas §12's positive "regularly sets aside" fits.

quiz.q: How does the treasury suffer under a king who fails to guard it?
options: he gives everything to ascetics until the treasury empties, the text opposing charity
neighbours plunder it
ministers embezzle all of it
he manages affairs sparsely and clumsily, leaves gates unsecured, and overspends on entertainers and gambling
quiz.why: The treatise blames poor management, unsecured gates, and spending beyond measure on entertainment and games. Master Cháng Bǎi: through board games and gambling he consumes the treasury without restraint, and he does not value it. Charity is never faulted.
